test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Heat Engine) Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The temperature of the air after compression stroke in a CI engine is:

options.text: high enough to auto-ignite the fuel without any external ignition source
high but not enough to ignite the fuel as spark plug is used to ignite the fuel

solution:
The correct answer is __high enough to auto-ignite the fuel without any external ignition source.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Compression Ignition (CI) engines__ operate based on the principle of air compression.
 
• During the compression stroke, the air is compressed to a high pressure and temperature.
 
• The temperature achieved is sufficient to ignite the injected fuel without the need for an external ignition source.
 
• This process is known as auto-ignition, and it is a characteristic feature of CI engines.
 
• The ignition of the fuel is controlled by the timing of fuel injection into the combustion chamber.
 
• The absence of spark plugs distinguishes CI engines from spark ignition (SI) engines.
 
• The high temperature is achieved due to the high compression ratio used in CI engines.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Spark Ignition (SI) Engines:**

 
 
• SI engines use a spark plug to ignite the air-fuel mixture.
 
• They operate on a comparatively lower compression ratio than CI engines.
 
 
 
• **Diesel Engines:**
 
 
• Diesel engines are a type of CI engine that uses diesel fuel for combustion.
 
• They are known for their higher thermal efficiency and fuel economy.
 
 
 
• **Compression Ratio:**
 
 
• The compression ratio is the ratio of the total volume to the clearance volume in the cylinder.
 
• CI engines typically have higher compression ratios than SI engines.
